description: AI consulting Karachi banks, insurers, traders and manufacturers can act on: ranked use cases, an AI policy that fits SBP and SECP rules, then a pilot.
h1: AI consulting Karachi firms can act on, not just read
intro: Our AI consultancy for Karachi companies finds the places where AI saves real time or money, ranks them by value and effort, and turns the best one into a working pilot. It suits established banks, insurers, trading houses, logistics firms and manufacturers that want AI used safely, inside SBP, SECP and PECA expectations.

sections.h: The problem: AI interest without a plan
p: By now, most Karachi boards have asked the question: what are we doing about AI? Usually the honest answer is a few staff using ChatGPT on personal accounts, a vendor demo nobody followed up, and an IT team that has been told to look into it on top of everything else.

That is risky in a city where so much of the work is confidential. A credit officer on I.I. Chundrigar Road pasting a customer file into a public chatbot, or a clearing agent uploading shipping documents to an unknown tool, creates exposure that nobody has signed off. Good AI consulting starts by finding out what is already happening, then deciding what should happen instead.

sections.h: What our AI consulting Karachi engagements include
list: AI readiness review: your data, systems, people and current AI use, written up in plain language.
Use-case discovery: workshops with each department, then a list of ideas ranked by value and effort.
AI roadmap: what to do in the next quarter, the next six months and later, with owners and dates.
Tool and vendor selection: build or buy, which models and platforms, and what they will cost to run.
AI policy and governance: who can use which tools, what data can go where, and how outputs are checked.
Data privacy review against PECA 2016 and the draft Personal Data Protection Bill.
Pilot build: one high-value use case built and tested with real users.
Team training in English or Urdu, for leadership and for the people who will use the tools daily.

sections.h: Where AI pays off in Karachi's economy
p: The best use cases depend on what your business does all day. In Karachi that tends to fall into a few patterns.
list: Banks and microfinance: summarising loan files, drafting credit memos, checking KYC documents and answering staff questions about internal policy.
Insurance: reading claim forms and survey reports, flagging missing documents and drafting first replies to policyholders.
Shipping and freight near Karachi Port and Port Qasim: extracting data from bills of lading, invoices and packing lists, and spotting mismatches before the goods declaration is filed.
FMCG and manufacturing: forecasting demand by distributor, analysing sales returns and summarising field-force reports.
Textile exporters: matching buyer purchase orders with production status and drafting compliance responses for international brands.
Retail and e-commerce: answering WhatsApp questions about stock, sizes and delivery, in Urdu and English.

sections.h: How it works: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: a short call to understand the business and the question behind it. If we are not the right fit, we say so on that call.
Plan: the readiness review and use-case workshops, ending with a written roadmap and an AI policy draft. You see the ranking logic, not just the result.
Build: we take the top use case and build a pilot with a small group of real users, measured against a baseline we agree in advance.
Grow: if the pilot works, we roll it out, train the wider team and move to the next item on the roadmap. If it does not, you find out quickly, before real money is spent, which is also useful.

sections.h: Regulation: what Karachi financial firms need to think about
p: For a bank or electronic money institution, the State Bank of Pakistan is the first question. Its outsourcing and cloud rules affect where a model runs, who processes the data and what the board must approve. For insurers, NBFCs and listed companies, SECP requirements on governance and reporting apply. PECA 2016 covers unauthorised access and misuse of data for everyone, and the Personal Data Protection Bill remains a draft, so we plan for its likely consent and data-handling principles without treating them as law.

Our AI consultancy does not replace your legal or compliance advice. It gives your compliance team a clear picture of each AI use case: what data it touches, where that data goes, and how a person checks the output before it reaches a customer.

sections.h: Proof from AI work we have done
p: We have delivered more than 30 AI builds: custom tools, systems and automations for businesses that used to run the old way. That matters for consulting, because our roadmaps are written by people who have built the things they recommend and know where the effort really goes.

We have no office in Karachi. The work is run from our London head office with one Signal Lead as your single point of contact. Our working day overlaps the Karachi afternoon: PKT is five hours ahead of London in winter and four in summer, so most workshops sit between 13:00 and 18:00 PKT.

Workshops run on video with each department in turn, and the materials come in writing afterwards. If a stage needs us in the room, for example a board session, we arrange a visit for that stage once it is agreed. Every date in the plan is confirmed in writing.
We scope every AI consultancy engagement individually and do not publish prices. The main cost factors are:
list: How many departments or business units are in scope.
The state of your data and whether it sits in one system or ten.
Whether you want a pilot built, and how complex it is.
Regulatory depth, for example SBP-regulated workloads that need extra documentation.
Training needs and the number of people to train.

faqs.q: What does an AI consultant do for a Karachi company?
faqs.a: An AI consultant finds where AI will save time or money in your business, ranks those ideas, and plans how to introduce them safely. For a Karachi company that usually means reviewing document-heavy work in finance, insurance, trade or manufacturing, writing an AI policy, choosing tools and building a first pilot with real users.

faqs.q: Is AI consulting Karachi banks use compatible with SBP rules?
faqs.a: It can be, if it is designed that way from the start. We map each use case to the data it handles and where processing happens, so your compliance team can test it against State Bank of Pakistan outsourcing and cloud requirements. Final approval sits with your compliance function and board, and we document everything they will need.

faqs.q: Do you meet Karachi clients in person?
faqs.a: Most of our work is remote from London, with video workshops during the London morning, which is the Karachi afternoon. We have no office or staff in Pakistan. If a stage of the project genuinely benefits from being in the room, such as a leadership workshop, we plan a visit for that stage with you.

faqs.q: Can AI tools work in Urdu?
faqs.a: Yes. Current large language models read and write Urdu, including Roman Urdu, with quality that varies by task. We test your actual documents and messages during the pilot, measure accuracy in both languages, and keep a person reviewing anything customer-facing until the results are consistently good enough.

faqs.q: How long does an AI consultancy engagement take?
faqs.a: A readiness review and roadmap for a mid-sized Karachi company typically takes a few weeks, depending on how many departments are involved and how quickly people are available for workshops. A pilot build adds more time. We agree the dates at the planning stage and put them in writing.

faqs.q: What if we already use ChatGPT or Copilot?
faqs.a: That is a useful starting point. We review how people are using them today, what data is going in, and whether the licences protect your information. Often the first win is moving staff from personal accounts to business accounts with a clear policy, then building targeted tools on top.

faqs.q: Do you only advise, or do you also build?
faqs.a: We build. Our consultancy ends with a working pilot, and the same team can take it into production as a custom AI tool, an automation or a feature in your app. That avoids the common gap where a strategy firm hands over a plan and a different vendor has to start again.
